_source: IEC 81346-2:2019, Table 1 (Entry classes), obtained from IEC's own free preview sample distributed via standards.iteh.ai (pages 1-15 of the publication, which include the front matter, scope, and Table 1 in full). This is the CURRENT edition (Edition 2.0, 2019-06) -- it replaced the 2009 edition and uses a materially different, more abstract classification scheme built on 'inherent function' rather than concrete device names.
_important_note: The 2019 standard explicitly warns: 'Any class is defined by its definition only. Users should select the appropriate class for their object to be classified based on the definition, and not rely upon the class name or the examples.' The popular informal folklore (K=relay, Q=breaker, S=switch, M=motor, T=transformer) that circulates in the electrical trade largely reflects older/pre-standard convention and the EARLIER 2009 edition, not this literal, function-based 2019 text. Both this file's 'official_definition' (verbatim-sourced) and its 'common_examples' (my own interpretation, applying the official definition to real device types -- NOT from the standard's own examples, which live in Table 3 at a page range beyond this 15-page preview) are provided so the gap between the two is visible rather than hidden.

classes.official_definition: object for picking up information and providing a representation
object for storing for subsequent retrieval
object for protecting against the effects of dangerous or undesirable conditions
object for providing a controllable flow
object for treating input signals and providing an appropriate output
object for providing mechanical movement or force
object for enclosing partly or fully another object
object for controlling access or flow
object for detecting a human action and providing an appropriate response
object for localising of other objects
object for leading from one place to another
